citeAs: Chen, C., Liu, M., Codella, N., Li, Y., Yuan, L., and Gurari, D. (2024). Fully Authentic Visual Question Answering Dataset from Online Communities. arXiv:2311.15562.
creator: Chongyan Chen, Mengchen Liu, Noel Codella, Yunsheng Li, Lu Yuan, Danna Gurari (University of Texas at Austin, Microsoft, University of Colorado Boulder)
description: VQAonline is the first Visual Question Answering dataset in which all contents originate from an authentic use case. Sourced from online question answering community forums (Stack Exchange), it contains 64,696 VQAs with authentic natural language questions, images, context, and answers validated by the individuals who asked the questions. It covers 105 diverse topics across five super-categories, with answers averaging 173 words in length.
name: VQAonline
publisher: University of Texas at Austin; Microsoft
rai:annotationsPerItem: For user intention annotations: 2 independent annotations per VQA (workers A and B), with a third annotation for tie-breaking (25 out of 105 cases). For domain expert evaluation: 6 model-answer ratings per VQA from one domain expert per topic.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Crowdworkers for user intention annotation: located in the United States, had completed more than 500 Human Intelligence Tasks (HITs) with over a 95% approval rating. Domain experts for human evaluation: ten individuals each with at least a Master's degree in a field related to their assigned VQA topic (Physical Fitness, Botany, Music, Mechanics, Politics, Law, Chinese Language, Economics, Statistics, and Artificial Intelligence); required to be located in the United States to guarantee English proficiency.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: For user intention taxonomy development, two annotators conducted four rounds of analysis on 105 visual questions. Agreement accuracy improved from 53.3% to 87.5% and Cohen's kappa improved from 45.24% to 84.69% across rounds. For the final crowdworker annotations, majority vote was used across 3 labels per VQA instance.
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Amazon Mechanical Turk (for user intention annotations); custom home-grown web-based interface (for domain expert human evaluation)
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: For user intention annotations: Three crowdworkers from Amazon Mechanical Turk were hired. Workers A and B each independently annotated 105 randomly selected VQAs (one per topic). When annotations disagreed (25 out of 105 cases), a third worker (C) broke the tie. Workers were provided instructions, taxonomy definitions, and two examples per user intention category. One-on-one Zoom training was provided, and a qualifying annotation test was required. For domain expert human evaluation: Ten domain experts (each with at least a Master's degree in a relevant field) were hired to rate model-generated answers as correct (1), partially correct (0.5), or incorrect (0) for 20 VQAs each across 10 topics, evaluating 6 model answers per VQA.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and the Internet. The geographic representation of Stack Exchange is unbalanced, with more users from countries like the US, India, and Europe and fewer from countries like Egypt. Additionally, 75 technology topics (e.g., Stack Overflow, LaTeX) were excluded because they typically involve language problems (questions about code shown in screenshots). Most models benchmarked on the dataset are believed to have been trained on Stack Exchange data, potentially giving them an unfair advantage.
rai:dataCollection: Data was scraped from the online question-answering platform Stack Exchange, using publicly-available data spanning from August 2010 to November 2022. The dataset collected all examples containing four components: a natural language question (post "title"), a natural language context (post "body"), an image (URL link), and at least one accepted answer. Only examples where the question poster marked an "accepted answer" were included. The Stack Exchange platform enforces a stringent reputation system with moderation policies and features topic-specific sites.
rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided URL link were removed from the dataset. This step reduced the dataset from 65,849 to 64,696 visual questions.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Raw data was sourced from the Stack Exchange archive hosted at https://archive.org/details/stackexchange in XML format. The initial candidate pool was 330,705 visual questions before filtering. Each raw example consisted of a post title (question), post body (context), image URL, and one or more answers from Stack Exchange users.
rai:dataLimitations: The dataset may poorly represent people in poverty-stricken areas since VQAs are posted by Stack Exchange users with access to mobile devices and the Internet. Geographic representation is unbalanced (more from US, India, Europe; less from countries like Egypt). The dataset excludes 75 technology topics (e.g., Stack Overflow, LaTeX) that typically involve code-related questions. Answers are considerably longer (mean 173 words) than existing VQA datasets, making standard VQA evaluation metrics ill-suited. Most benchmarked models may have been trained on Stack Exchange data, complicating fair evaluation.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Two filtering steps were applied: (1) Removed visual questions with scores of 0 or less for either the question or answer (using Stack Exchange's up-vote/down-vote system). (2) Excluded visual questions with multiple images (e.g., GIFs) or with visual answers. Additionally, examples for which the image could not be downloaded from the provided URL link were removed. For data format consistency, all images were converted to PNG format. Starting from 330,705 candidates, after removing those without accepted answers (165,766 remained), then low-score items (119,177), then multiple-image items (85,573), then visual-answer items (65,849), then undownloadable images, the final dataset of 64,696 VQAs was obtained.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is expected to benefit many real-world applications including other community question answering platforms (e.g., Yahoo! Answers, Wiki Answers, Quora), learning assistance VQA tools for children, virtual assistants, visual dialog and query, as well as visual search and browsing. The dataset facilitates research community progress in improving VQA models for authentic use cases. It also enables exploration of the hallucination issue in authentic use cases. The dataset may underrepresent people in poverty-stricken areas and has unbalanced geographic representation.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and improving VQA models for authentic use cases; few-shot learning research; evaluation metric development for long-form text answers; community question answering platforms (e.g., Yahoo! Answers, Wiki Answers, Quora); learning assistance VQA tools for children; virtual assistants; visual dialog and query; visual search and browsing; multilingual VQA research; text VQA research; hallucination research in vision-language models.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-3.5 was used via zero-shot prompting to bootstrap user intention categories (indicating user intentions given a question and context). DeepSolo (state-of-the-art text spotter model) was used to detect text presence in all images in the dataset, finding that 76% (48,161 images) contain text.
rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset is sourced from publicly posted content on Stack Exchange. No explicit collection of personally identifiable information is described. The dataset includes multilingual VQAs and covers users from various countries, but no specific PII collection is mentioned.

null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation of missing values is described; missing images were simply removed from the dataset.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection augmentation, balancing, or resampling of the dataset itself is described beyond the filtering steps already captured in preprocessing.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning, update cadence, or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
